chunks: Al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from Amr ibn Yahya who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed facing a direction other than the Qibla, then the Qibla became clear to him, and the time for another prayer had already entered. He said: 'He must repeat it before he prays this one whose time has entered.'

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.يُعِيدُهَا: He repeats it (referring to the prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they realize they prayed in the wrong direction after the time for the next prayer has started?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the validity of prayer when the Qibla is initially misidentified. The Imam specifies that if the time for a subsequent prayer has already entered, the erroneous prayer must be repeated *before* commencing the new one, ensuring the integrity of the missed obligation is rectified first. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the sequential order of obligations when time constraints overlap.
